course_name_original: Fundamentos de Control de Procesos Industriales
prerequisites: Having completed the basic training modules, common to the industrial branch and specific to Industrial Electronic and Automatic Engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals of complex industrial process control.
Participate in the development of industrial installation projects.
Define the necessary process control elements.
Define technical and functional specifications for industrial processes.
Select the most suitable technologies for use in the manufacturing process.

syllabus_topics: Industrial process automation. Representation standards (P&ID, Flow diagrams). System integration.
Digital process control technologies. Discrete control. System identification. Introduction to adaptive control.
Steelmaking process control. Control systems in different stages of the steelmaking process.

Laboratory exercises with laboratory equipment and simulation, covering concepts of control system design and automation in industrial environments, system identification, digital control, and design of control architectures complementary to those seen in previous courses.

assessment_methods.method: Block 1 (T1) works and reports (including lab exercises, code and simulations)
Block 2 (T2) works and reports (including lab exercises, code and simulations)
Block 3 (T3) works, reports and oral presentation

assessment_rules: For ordinary calls, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required for each of the three thematic blocks (T1, T2, T3). If the minimum grade is achieved in each part, the final grade is calculated as 0.2 x T1 + 0.35 x T2 + 0.35 x T3 + 0.1 x A. Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. Formal aspects, authorship, and authorized means will be considered. For extraordinary calls, the evaluation is similar, maintaining the active participation grade and replacing oral presentations with individual explanations of work.
